# Figure provenance

**Every image in this repository was generated by our own code. None was
downloaded, none is stock art, and none was traced or copied from a paper.**

That is a checkable claim, not an assertion — run `python verify_figures.py`
from this folder.

---

## The evidence

A PNG file carries a `tEXt` metadata chunk. Matplotlib stamps its own name and
version into it on every save. Every PNG in this repository carries:

```
Software: 'Matplotlib version3.10.9, https://matplotlib.org/'
```

An image downloaded from a paper, a website, or a stock library would carry
something else entirely — an EXIF block from a camera, an Adobe or GIMP
signature, or no `Software` chunk at all. None of ours does. `verify_figures.py`
reads the chunk out of every file and fails loudly on anything that is not
matplotlib-generated.

This is worth caring about because a figure lifted from a paper is a copyright
problem *and* an academic-integrity problem, and "we made it ourselves" is
hard to prove after the fact unless you can point at something concrete.

| `fig11_real_spectra61.png` | **Data** | ✅ `real_mof_band.ipynb`, Step 9 | `3_notebooks/real_results.json` — all 61 spectra + ranking |
| `fig01_mof_concept.png` | Schematic | ⚠️ script not preserved | None — a drawn diagram: node + linker → framework |
| `fig02_pipeline.png` | Schematic | ⚠️ script not preserved | None — the pipeline stages, drawn |
| `fig05_defect.png` | **Data** | ⚠️ script not preserved | `1_website/HKUST-1.cif`, λ₂ before and after removing a linker |
| `fig06_boxgrowing.png` | **Data** | ⚠️ script not preserved | `1_website/HKUST-1.cif`, box-growing curves |

**Being straight about the ⚠️ rows.** Those four were generated during earlier
work by scripts that were not committed. They are verifiably matplotlib output
— `verify_figures.py` confirms it — and the numbers in them are reproduced
independently by the live site, which computes the same quantities in the
browser. But we cannot currently regenerate the *image* with one command, and
saying otherwise would be exactly the kind of unverifiable claim this document
exists to avoid. Bringing them into `make_figures.py` is a known task.

"Schematic" means the figure explains an idea rather than plotting a
measurement — the shapes and positions are chosen for clarity. They are drawn
in matplotlib, not clip art. Everything marked **Data** plots numbers our
pipeline computed, and the input is named so you can check it.

### A bug this caught

Writing `make_figures.py` immediately exposed an error. The first draft built
its own quotient graph and reported coordination numbers of 8, 48, 12 and 4 for
the four structures — every one exactly **double** the published value, because
it counted *bonds* rather than *distinct neighbours*, and a carboxylate linker
grips a metal node through two oxygen atoms.

The fix was to stop reimplementing and call `code_09_network_analysis`, the
implementation already validated against crystallography and cross-checked
against the independent JavaScript engine. A figure drawn from a second,
unvalidated implementation is not evidence about the first — it is only a
second chance to be wrong.

## The duplicates are deliberate

The same figure appears in more than one folder:

| File | Copies in | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `fig01`–`fig08` | `1_website/figures/`, `8_textbook/figures/` | The site must work from a `file://` clone with no build step, and the textbook must render on GitHub. Neither can reach across folders reliably, so each carries its own copy. |
| `band77_figure.png` | `4_reference/`, `7_presentation/`, `7_presentation/overleaf/` | LaTeX resolves `\includegraphics` relative to the `.tex` file, and the Overleaf zip has to be self-contained when uploaded. |
| `fig09_real_vs_hmof.png` | `4_reference/`, `1_website/figures/`, `8_textbook/figures/`, `7_presentation/`, `7_presentation/overleaf/` | Same reasons: the site needs a local copy, and LaTeX needs one beside the `.tex`. |

### One figure was deleted

`band_analysis.png` was removed in September 2026. It showed a Δα band of
**0.835–0.941** built from eight named MOFs — HKUST-1, ZIF-8 and six MOF-74
variants. That band predates the 77-framework analysis and contradicts it: the
current hypothetical band is 1.02–1.41 and the synthesised one is 0.95–1.47.

It was also the thing this project explicitly stopped doing — defining a band
from a handful of demonstration structures. Leaving a superseded figure on the
Results page would have shown a reviewer three mutually inconsistent bands. It
is replaced by `fig08_band77.png`, which plots all 77.

The duplicates are byte-identical copies of one generated file, not separately
produced images that could drift apart. `verify_figures.py` checks that by
hashing every copy.

## Regenerating

```bash
cd 4_reference
pip install numpy matplotlib
python make_figures.py          # regenerate into 4_reference/
python make_figures.py --sync   # ...and copy to 1_website/ and 8_textbook/
```

This regenerates fig03, fig04, fig07 and `network_analysis_figure.png` from the
live pipeline — not from stored numbers. If the pipeline changes, so do they.

`fig08_band77.png` comes from the analysis notebook rather than this script,
because it plots all 77 spectra and needs the full `results.json`:

```bash
jupyter notebook ../3_notebooks/mof_band_analysis.ipynb   # Step 11
```

After regenerating, copy the outputs to the folders listed in the duplicates
table above, or run `python make_figures.py --sync` which does it for you.

---

## Verifying

```bash
cd 4_reference
python verify_figures.py
```

It checks three things and exits non-zero on any failure:

1. **Every PNG was produced by matplotlib** — reads the `Software` chunk.
2. **No PNG carries camera or image-editor metadata** — the signature of a
   downloaded or retouched image.
3. **Duplicated figures are byte-identical** — so a stale copy in one folder
   cannot silently disagree with the live one in another.


---

## A figure that was drawn but could not be trusted

The analysis notebook emits `real_vs_hypothetical.png`. When the 61-structure run
was executed on its own, the 77-framework `results.json` was not in the session,
so the figure came out titled **"Spectrum width: synthesised vs hypothetical"**
with only the synthesised row drawn.

Nothing about it was corrupt. It was worse than that: the title asserted a
comparison the picture did not contain, and a reader skimming the deck would
have taken the single row as the comparison. It is not shipped.
`make_real_band_figures.py` redraws it from both files, and fails loudly if
either is missing.

This is the same class of error as the deleted `band_analysis.png` above — a
figure whose caption outran its data — and it is the reason every figure in this
folder has to name the file it was computed from.
